Duties include but not limited to: Functions as liaison and is responsible for planning, coordinating, and performing a wide range of clinical, administrative , program, and technical functions to support quality case manage of sex specific services for veterans.

Works directly, with the patients, VA staff, non-VA care provides and organizations, Radiology Departments, and the Women Veterans Program Manager to achieve seamless care, facilitate patient satisfaction, reduce duplication of services or delay of care, and monitor quality of care and services received.

Responsible and accountable for the provision of direct and indirect care and for the delivery of quality nursing care to a culturally Veteran population. Provides care and counseling of persons to promote and maintain health.

Coordinating and tracking sex specific care (i.e., breast care/mammography, gynecological coordination, maternity care, etc.) of patients throughout all aspects of the medical center, including Community Based Outpatient Clinics, as well as community vendors and or agencies.

Assists with initial VA consult referrals for gynecology, mammography, non-VA care, and/or other care assisting with VA or community services for the patient with an appropriate provider, to include coordinating any subsequent appointments or follow ups, as needed.

Educates patients on a variety of sex specific topics, to include importance of routine medical screenings. Assists veterans who have presented to VA or non VA emergency department for gender specific emergencies, to secure appropriate follow up care such as a lab, ultrasound, emotional support, and/or other care as needed.

Coordinates care with the Veterans Patient Aligned Care Team (PACT). Documents patient care interactions accurately, succinctly, and timely, using appropriate notes, templates, and clinical reminders, in the electronic medical record.

Manages appropriate use of the electronic alert (flag) for breast breast and cervical screenings, and/or other issues in the electronic medical record. Understands and responds to mammography reports, BIRADS, Pap and other sex specific screening/diagnostic test results. Documents communication of the test results for female specific testing.

Contacts patients who fail to keep mammogram appointments, or who are delinquent in obtaining recommended breast cancer or other diagnostic screenings (i.e., Pap), to determine and resolve obstacles the veteran may have with keeping appointments.

Participates in quality improvement programs and initiatives including system redesign, to improve access, quality efficiency, and patient satisfaction.

Nurse I, Level II Demonstrates integration of biopsychosocial concepts, cognitive skills and technically competent practice in providing care to clients with basic or complex.

Self-directed in goal setting for managing complex client situations.

Utilization of safe patient handling and mobility protocols.

The Cancer Care Navigator Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based care to assigned patients. Provides patient management, care coordination, and disposition planning for cancer patients.

The Cancer Care Navigator assists Veterans, family members, and caregivers with receiving the most appropriate options and services to meet their complex health care needs. Coordinates care with multiple providers across all levels and sites of care.

Coordination also includes assuring services interface within the Veterans Affairs (VA) and community programs to provide continuity of care to patients.

Provides oversight of the patient's journey through the diagnostic and treatment continuum, ensuring that all steps in the process are scheduled, timely and completed, while tracking the overall treatment plan.

They will follow select patients from the earliest suspicion of cancer through the continuum of cancer care including diagnosis, treatment, survivorship/surveillance, or palliation/end of life.

The Cancer Care Navigator will interface with outside referral agencies and ensure that their business and clinical practices are in compliance with regulatory standards. Anticipates and implements preventive patient care measures.

Possesses the ability to assess data reflective of the patient's status and interpret the appropriate information needed to identify each patient's requirements relative to their age-specific needs, providing care as considered necessary.

Provides guidance and education to patients and caregivers and collaborates with other professionals at all levels. Addresses psychosocial, as well as nursing and medical needs of patients and their families/caregivers, through participation with the interdisciplinary care team.

Ensures the plan of care and educational requirements are individualized and tailored specifically to support each individual patient's needs. Reports status of service needs and contributes to problem resolution and modification of processes as necessary. Evaluates care and outcomes to ensure timely and appropriate provision of services.

Advocates for holistic care through patient/family education and provider interaction and implements an educational plan to meet the patient care needs. The Cancer Care Navigator demonstrates leadership in delivering and improving holistic care through collaborative strategies with others.

Evaluates practice in an ongoing process, based on best evidence. Provides peers with informal constructive feedback for improvement. Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of healthcare professionals. Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team.

Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes. Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care. Shares educational findings, experiences, and ideas with peers. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care.

Participates in activities and strategies to sustain evidence-based-practice.

The Quality Management Department reports to the Medical Center Director and is responsible for providing an impartial and forthright review of the entire Medical Center's preparation and performance for accreditation reviews and overall quality of patient care to the Medical Center's executive leadership.

The Accreditation Specialist (AS) reports to the Deputy Director of Quality Management and is accountable to the Director of Quality Management.

The AS promotes the medical center mission, vision, and values, complies with the Equal Employment Opportunity programs, partnerships, customer service standards and Veterans Affairs policies and procedures and works with internal and external customers to the Quality Management Department to support these goals and successes.

Collaborates with leadership and colleagues to complete all other duties as assigned.

The Accreditation Program requirements include, but are not limited to, developing and coordinating internal review systems to assure that both clinical and administrative programs follow agency and accrediting standards and regulatory requirements, utilizes databases to improve performance and outcome measures, identifying trends and opportunities for improvement in performance and collaborating with the clinicians throughout the Medical Center to understand the processes that support the metrics and how to develop improvement plans for sustainment of those metrics.

The AS is responsible for translating regulatory and accrediting body standards, policies, and strategies into action within the complex interrelationships that exist in a health care environment as it applies to program oversight areas.

The Quality Management Accreditation Nurse contributes to the overall success of the Quality Management Department by providing expert oversight and direction on all accreditation program activities, which includes preparation and post-review improvement activities through collaborating and providing feedback on any clinical or administrative practice or process within the Medical Center surrounding program requirements and alignment with the numerous accreditation organizations who provide oversight for the organization.

The Quality Management Accreditation Nurse is expected to be self-directed and self-managing in performance of their daily activities. The Quality Management Accreditation Nurse serves as a liaison, representing the facility accreditation program, to the Veterans Integrated System Network (VISN).

The AS serves as the primary point of contact for VISN requests and participates in VISN activities. The AS is required to communicate and maintain positive relationships with other departments and agencies, both within and outside of the Lebanon VAMC.

Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/. Physical Requirements: The population of male and female Veterans served ranges from the adult, age 18, to the elderly adult, age 65 and over.

This position requires visual acuity, keen hearing, clear distinctive speech, and manual dexterity. This position requires potentially long periods of continued walking, standing, stooping, sitting, bending, pulling, and pushing, lifting 45 pounds or more, reaching, stretching, and similar activities supporting various weights.

Transferring patients and objects may be required. The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations or operative/invasive procedures.

The incumbent may occasionally be exposed to patients who are combative secondary to delirium, dementia, or psychiatric disorders. The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on patient needs.

The incumbent must complete annual employee health requirements as a condition of employment. These physical requirements will be consistent with VA Directive Handbook 5019.

Provide direct and indirect patient care, ensuring adherence to established nursing standards, policies, and procedures. Conduct comprehensive nursing assessments, identify patient needs, and develop individualized care plans in collaboration with the healthcare team, Veterans, and their families.

Administer medications and treatments as prescribed, monitor patient responses, and take appropriate action in accordance with VA guidelines. Educate Veterans and their families on health conditions, medications, treatment plans, and self-care strategies to promote optimal health outcomes.

Maintain accurate, timely, and thorough electronic health records (EHR) documentation. Utilize critical thinking skills to anticipate and respond to changes in patient conditions, initiating appropriate interventions and escalating concerns as necessary. Participate in interdisciplinary team meetings to ensure coordinated and holistic patient care.

Adhere to all safety protocols and infection control practices. Serve as a patient advocate, ensuring ethical considerations and Veterans' rights are respected. Engage in continuous professional development and participate in quality improvement initiatives.

The Assistant Nurse Manager (ANM's) Functions as a clinical expert and is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing or supervising direct patient care. Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates delivery of care based on age specific components.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team and creating innovative process improvement initiatives.

Functions as a role model, educator, practitioner, and supervisor providing leadership to the team. Enhances care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team to remove barriers and implement new evidence-based cutting-edge programs/processes.

The ANM engages in professional organizations to enhance leadership and career growth. Adheres to ethical principles in decision-making, fostering accountability at personal, organizational, and staff levels. Equips staff with tools for competent care and promotes an environment of accountability for high-quality, cost-effective outcomes.

This is a Temporary Not to exceed one year, Intermittent Position. The Med-Surg Float Pool RN must demonstrate strong clinical judgment and adaptability to changing work environments, with flexibility in patient care assignments.

Care is ongoing and covers various stages of recuperation, from diagnosis to treatment and health promotion, recovery, or end-of-life care.

Goals are achieved through prompt detection of emergencies, prevention of complications, diagnostic and therapeutic procedures, patient and family education to improve self-care, health maintenance and rehabilitation, and facilitating discharge from acute care.

The RN participates in continuous improvement initiatives, professional governance, and High Reliability Organization (HRO) models as part of personal and professional development.

Major Duties include but are not limited to: Flexibility in patient care assignment Care for boarding patients in temporary bed locations Interpretation of Continuous Telemetry monitored patients can be trained upon hire Diabetic management and teaching Management of gastric intestinal and/or percutaneous drainage and feeding tubes Administration & Monitoring Medications Skills in time management, priority setting, assessment, and urgent intervention are essential for this unit.

Duties are but not limited to: The RN identifies and addresses communication and workflow challenges, collaborates with leadership and associated stakeholders, and schedules meetings among teams. Follows procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

The Nurse PACT Coordinator is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based practices. Validates understanding of the rationale for PACT care processes and decisions. Questions clinical practices for the purpose of providing evidence-based care. Demonstrates the ability to cope with and manage competing priorities.

Integrates knowledge, skills, abilities, and judgment and is self-directed in goal setting for managing complex situations. The nurse demonstrates competence in practice and decision-making, deliberate planning, and critical thinking skills. Executes position to promote full PACT implementation and function within the Primary Care setting.

Focuses on the implementation and sustainment of the PACT model driven by quality improvement and evidence-based decision-making. Interacts with and assists PACT members in achieving compliance with Veterans Affairs Central Office (VACO), Veteran Integrated Services Network (VISN), and local policies and directives.

Assists teams to maintain national Primary Care standards using clinical practice guidelines and clinical pathways. Promotes PACT fundamentals. Conducts knowledge sharing to provide safe, efficient, quality PACT care. Fosters a safe and supportive environment of care.

Delivers self-directed, professional nursing practice using the nursing process (assessment, diagnosis, outcome identification, planning, implementation, and evaluation) for complex patients based on conscious and deliberate planning with occasional supervision. Expectations: 1.

Uses knowledge of PACT principles to support PACT team care delivery, resulting in positive impact/improvement. Outcomes clearly demonstrated. 2. Assists core PACT teams in organizing care delivery. 3. Monitors fidelity to the PACT model of care. Monitors outcomes. Offers focused training and education relating to the PACT model of care. 4.

Independently plans and delivers technically competent care to patients with complex needs in alignment with the ANA Standards of Nursing Practice. 5. Manages the care of patients, while organizing and prioritizing patient care needs, and ensuring assigned tasks are completed. 6.

Functions as an emerging leader in providing direction to staff to identify, implement and evaluate patient care needs. 7. Collaborates with the interdisciplinary team to ensure the plan of care is achieved.

Preferred Experience: 3-5 years PACT experience, Chronic Disease Management, ability to create excel data spreadsheets, Charge Nurse experience, ability to analyze data, educate staff on performance measure to meet eQM and SAIL metrics by utilizing multiple databases, develop and complete data reports utilizing excel and PowerPoint presentations.

The Emergency Department (ED) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities that demonstrate leadership, experience, and creative approaches to management of complex patient care. Collaborates in the development, implementation, evaluation, and revision of policies, procedures, and/or guidelines.

Provides urgent and emergent care to patients with acute and/or chronic medical, surgical, and psychiatric conditions. Nursing care ranges from basic nursing care to stabilization, resuscitation, and life support measures. Emergency nursing practice is independent and collaborative.

The ED RN practice includes the roles of direct care provider, educator, administrator, researcher, consultant, leader, and advocate. Provides peers with formal or informal constructive feedback for improvement. Supports colleagues and other nurses through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality nursing care.

Fosters a safe and supportive environment conducive to the professional development of health care professionals. Evaluates outcomes of evidence-based decisions and practice changes for individuals, groups, and populations. Responsible for the documented outcomes at the program or service level.

Program or service level outcomes must be broad and complex and can be demonstrated at any organizational level within a facility. The ED RN is responsible and accountable for all elements of the nursing process when providing care.

They assess the patient by collecting pertinent data or information, including the triage of patients based on the five-level triage system to prioritize patients that require more immediate care. They use the assessment data to determine diagnoses, problems, or other concerns.

They will identify expected outcomes to develop a collaborative and individualized plan for each patient. The ED RN will implement that plan, including care coordination, health teaching, and health promotion. They evaluate the progress toward achieving the expected goal and outcomes and adjusts the plan as necessary.

## L'entreprise : HUG ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour découvrir les moments forts et chiffres clefs de l'année 2025 en cliquant ici.
Comptant près de 1'200 collaboratrices et collaborateurs, le Département de médecine aiguë (D-MA) inclut les Services d'anesthésiologie, de pharmacologie et toxicologie cliniques, des soins intensifs et des urgences.

Il répond à une quadruple mission au travers de ses services qui apportent leur expertise en interaction fréquente avec l'ensemble des Hôpitaux universitaires de Genève, grâce à un plateau transversal, dans l'objectif d'assurer la meilleure prise en charge possible des patients et patientes.
Le Service d'anesthésiologie est un service transversal des HUG au cœur du plateau technique. Avec ses 8 unités médicales et une unité de recherche et d'innovation, sa mission vise à assurer le confort et la sécurité des patientes et patients au cours d'actes thérapeutiques ou diagnostiques, médicaux ou chirurgicaux, ainsi que lors des soins post-interventionnels, tout en veillant à la bonne prise en charge de la douleur.
Plus grand centre de Suisse en nombres d'actes interventionnels assumés par année, le Service d'anesthésiologie est à la pointe des progrès réalisés dans ce domaine. Le service pourvoit également l'enseignement pré- et post-gradué et continu des infirmiers et infirmières, et des médecins en formation spécialisée.

Service de prestations, l'anesthésiologie intervient également dans le domaine de l'antalgie interventionnelle et dans des situations d'urgences vitales intrahospitalières ou préhospitalières aux côtés du Service des urgences.

## Description du poste ##
Vous assurez la prise en soins globale des patients et patientes, durant leur séjour dans les unités de soins péri-interventionnelles du Service d'anesthésie en collaboration avec les intervenants et intervenantes internes et externes.
Vous accueillez, accompagnez et prodiguez des soins à une patientèle nécessitant une surveillance continue, monitorée dans différentes salles de surveillances post-interventionnelles, avec une intensification du traitement dans une unité de soins intermédiaires péri-interventionnelle.
Vous promouvez et développez les soins infirmiers au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire.
Vous garantissez la sécurité du patient et de la patiente et réalisez des prestations de qualité dans un environnement de soins aigus.
Votre périmètre de travail peut inclure d'autres unités d'Anesthésiologie (Accueil ambulatoire, Antalgie interventionnelle, etc.).
## Description du profil ##
Vous êtes en possession d'un Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers ou d'un diplôme en soins infirmiers reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous avez travaillé dans un service de soins aigus ou suivi une formation certifiante (Certificat en soins intermédiaires).
Vous possédez des compétences confirmées dans la pratique des soins. Une expérience en soins aigus est indispensable.
Vous faites preuve de disponibilité et de ponctualité. Vous êtes apte à promouvoir la qualité des soins et à travailler tant de manière autonome que dans une équipe pluridisciplinaire.
Vous possédez d'excellentes capacités d'analyse, de synthèse, d'organisation, de gestion des priorités et de résistance au stress.
Vous êtes une personne ouverte aux changements et à la remise en question de vos pratiques.
Vous avez de l'aisance dans les relations humaines et possédez une forte capacité d'écoute et d'empathie.
Vous vous engagez à suivre une formation certifiante (Certificat en soins intermédiaires).

Weiterbildung zur Dipl. Expertin/Experte Intensivpflege NDS HF
==============================================================
In den beiden Einheiten, bestehend aus der Neonatologie\-Intensivstation und der Neonatologie\-IMC mit insgesamt 11 Plätzen, erwartet Sie das gesamte neonatologische Spektrum. Wir arbeiten auf den Pflegestationen nach den Leanprinzipien. Visuelles Management, Arbeitsnivellierung und kontinuierliche Verbesserung stehen für uns dabei im Vordergrund.
Weiterbildung zur Dipl. Expertin/Experte Intensivpflege NDS HF
==============================================================
**Neonatologie/Pädiatrie**
100%
nach Vereinbarung, unbefristet
**Ihre Aufgaben**
* Beim zweijährigen berufsbegleitendem Nachdiplomstudium zur/zum Dipl. Expertin/Experte Intensivpflege NDS HF mit Schwerpunkt Pädiatrie / Neonatologie, betreuen Sie komplex erkrankte Säuglinge und Frühgeborene ab der 23 Schwangerschaftswoche.
* Sie sind bei internen und externen Abholtransporten mit der Ambulanz, sowie bei REGA\-Transporten im In\-und Ausland dabei.
* Sie schätzen die Herausforderung, mit komplexen und sich schnell ändernden Situationen umzugehen und meistern diese mit professionellem Geschick.
* Das Teaching und Coaching wird von der Berufsbildung und die Begleitung durch Fachpersonen übernommen. Als Studierende/r sind Sie im ersten und vierten Semester auf der Neonatologie KSA AG und im zweiten und dritten Semester auf der Intensivstation vom Universitäts\-Kinderspital Zürich eingeteilt.
* Die theoretische Bildung erfolgt durch den Bildungsanbieter Z\-INA (Höherer Fachschule Intensiv\-, Notfall\- und Anästhesiepflege in Zürich).
**Ihr Profil**
* Sie sind eine Dipl. Pflegefachperson HF/FH oder haben ein vom SBFI anerkanntes ausländisches Diplom in der Pflege und eine Berufserfahrung von mindestens 6 Monaten im Akutpflegebereich.
* Sie sind eine engagierte, aufgeschlossene Persönlichkeit und empfinden wechselnde Situationen und die interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit als interessante Herausforderung.
* Sie besitzen das C1 Sprachniveau.

Accueil**Infirmier(-ère) de jour en Médecine - CDM 6 mois à 60%**
Particulièrement reconnu pour son approche diagnostic rapide et pour la qualité des soins, le service de médecine interne a un rôle central au sein de notre établissement. Il a pour mission de recevoir des patients sans diagnostic, souvent référés par le service des urgences.
Dans un contexte de développement de nouvelles filières de soins, notamment en gériatrie et en soins palliatifs, notre service est appelé à évoluer et à renforcer ses compétences dans la prise en charge de patients âgés, poly morbides et présentant des situations de soins complexes.
Afin de compléter notre service nous** recrutons un/e**
**Infirmier(-ère) de jour en Médecine - CDM 6 mois à 60% (ref : 2013)**
**Votre mission :**
Dans un établissement de pointe vous occupez un poste varié au sein d'une équipe pluridisciplinaire comprenant des infirmiers(-ères), des aides-soignants(-es), des médecins.
Vous devrez assurer l-accueil des patients atteints de pathologies polyvalentes, dans le cadre d-une prise en charge globale en phase aigüe.
A ce titre vous êtes en charge de ;
* Installer le patient et lui présenter les informations d'organisation administrative et de soin
* Recueillir et transmettre les données médicales et administratives et compléter le dossier de soins informatisé
* Assurer et organiser la planification des soins en fonction des priorités et du degré d'urgence
* Effectuer les soins sur prescription médicale et en conformité avec les procédures de l-unité et institutionnelles
* Assurer la tenue du Dossier Patient Informatisé
* Evaluer continuellement l'état clinique du patient et son évolution en situation aigue
* Identifier les situations de fragilité, de perte d'autonomie et de complexité nécessitant une approche interdisciplinaire ;
* Participer à la prise en charge de patients âgés et polymorbides, ainsi qu'à l'accompagnement de patients et de leurs proches confrontés à des situations palliatives ;
* Collaborer avec les différents intervenants afin d'assurer la continuité et la coordination des soins ;
* Assurer la coordination inter services pour la gestion des mouvements de patients
* Coordonner les entrées et sorties : les mutations internes, les transferts externes des patients en collaboration avec le cadre de santé.
**Nous recherchons un profil répondant aux critères suivants :**
* Diplôme d'infirmier(-ère)
* En possession de la reconnaissance croix rouge si diplôme étranger
* Disposant d'une expérience en médecine interne, en gériatrie, en soins palliatifs ou dans un domaine de soins complexes, un atout ;
* Présentant un intérêt marqué pour la prise en charge des patients âgés, polymorbides et/ou en situation palliative ;
* Sensible à l'approche globale et interdisciplinaire du patient ;
* Sens du contact et du service dans le cadre d'un établissement privé
* Autonome, bienveillance, polyvalence, capacité d'adaptation, d'organisation et sens des priorités sont des qualités essentielles
* Attitude positive au sein d'une équipe et êtes capable de générer un climat de confiance
* Capable de contribuer à instaurer un climat de confiance avec les patients, leurs proches et les différents professionnels.

The Specialty Care Outpatient Staff Registered Nurse (RN) is responsible for providing competent, evidence-based specialty care to assigned patients and oversight of licensed vocational nurses/nursing assistants, as appropriate to the clinic setting.

This nurse provides patient care, care coordination, health promotion, health education and coaching on wellness, disease prevention, and chronic care management. Administers medications and procedures per established policies and guidelines. Influences care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team.

Contributes professional nursing perspective in discussions with the interdisciplinary team. Partners with others to effect change and produce optimal outcomes.

Supports colleagues through knowledge sharing to provide safe, quality specialty nursing care.
